paragraphs.title: Transmitting the Command and the Sanctity of Speech

easy.explanation: Numbers 30:1 says that Moses spoke unto the heads of the tribes.
easy.q: To whom did Moses speak concerning the command of the LORD?

answers: This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded
easy.explanation: The verse introduces the command with the words, “This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded.”
easy.q: What did Moses say the LORD had commanded?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth.”
easy.q: What must a person do with what proceeds out of his mouth?

medium.explanation: The verse teaches that a person must not break a vow or oath spoken before the LORD.
medium.q: What does the phrase “he shall not break his word” teach?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes binding oneself through a vow or oath.
medium.q: What is the meaning of “to bind his soul with a bond”?

answers: The people speak to Moses, then Moses speaks to God
The LORD commands Moses, and Moses speaks to the tribal leaders
The tribal leaders command the LORD
medium.explanation: The LORD gives the command, and Moses conveys it to the heads of the tribes.
medium.q: What is the order of communication in these verses?

answers: A person should speak carefully before making a vow
A person may promise without keeping it
Only rulers are responsible for their words
challenge.explanation: Because spoken vows are binding, a person should consider his words carefully.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the command to do all that proceeds from one’s mouth?

answers: They were important recipients of the command
challenge.explanation: Moses addressed the tribal leaders as important recipients of the LORD’s instruction.
challenge.q: Why are the heads of the tribes specifically mentioned?

challenge.explanation: Both a vow and an oath bind the person who speaks them.
challenge.q: What do a vow and an oath have in common in these verses?

paragraphs.title: A Woman’s Vows in Her Father’s House and at Betrothal

answers: In her father’s house in her youth
easy.explanation: Verse 4 describes a woman being in her father’s house in her youth.
easy.q: Where is the young woman when she makes her vow?

easy.explanation: If her father remains silent, all her vows and bonds shall stand.
easy.q: What happens if her father hears her vow and holds his peace?

answers: Make it of none effect or allow it to stand
easy.explanation: The husband may disallow the vow on the day he hears it; otherwise it stands.
easy.q: What may a husband do when he hears his wife’s vow?

medium.explanation: The KJV says that none of her vows or bonds shall stand if her father disallows them that day.
medium.q: What happens if the father disallows the vow on the day he hears it?

answers: To reject or cancel its effect
To forget that it was spoken
medium.explanation: In this context, to disallow a vow is to reject it so that it does not stand.
medium.q: What does “disallow” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: Verse 7 says, “then her vows shall stand.”
medium.q: What happens when the husband hears the vow and holds his peace?

answers: The cancellation must occur on the day it is heard
The cancellation must occur years later
The cancellation must occur before the vow is spoken
challenge.explanation: In both cases, the vow may be disallowed on the day the father or husband hears it.
challenge.q: What condition is shared by the father’s and husband’s power to cancel a vow?

answers: The time of hearing is important
The time of hearing does not matter
The vow is valid only at night
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes the day of hearing as the time when the vow may be upheld or canceled.
challenge.q: What does the repeated timing phrase “in the day that he heareth” emphasize?

answers: Her father always remains the authority
The husband becomes the authority described in the passage
challenge.explanation: After the passage describes a woman in her father’s house, it describes the husband’s authority over her vow.
challenge.q: What changes when the woman is described as having a husband?

paragraphs.title: The Vows of a Widow, Divorced Woman, and Married Woman

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says that every vow of a widow or divorced woman shall stand against her.
easy.q: What happens to the vow of a widow or divorced woman?

easy.explanation: The passage gives the husband authority concerning certain vows of his wife.
easy.q: Who may establish or make void certain vows of a married woman?

answers: The vows pass to her father
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “then all her vows shall stand.”
easy.q: What happens if the husband hears the vow and does not disallow it?

answers: The widow’s or divorced woman’s vow stands, while the husband has authority concerning a married woman’s vow
A married woman cannot make vows
A widow’s vow is always canceled by her father
medium.explanation: The verses say that the vow of a widow or divorced woman stands, while a husband may establish or make void certain vows.
medium.q: What is the main difference between a widow or divorced woman and a married woman in these verses?

answers: A vow involving self-denial or personal affliction
A vow that cannot be spoken aloud
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a vow involving affliction or restraint of oneself.
medium.q: What does “to afflict the soul” describe in this passage?

answers: It concerns vows and binding oaths described in the passage
He has no connection to the vows
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says that the husband may establish or make void every vow and binding oath to afflict the soul.
medium.q: What limitation of the husband’s authority is shown in verse 14?

answers: To show that the passage does not name a husband who can make them void
To teach that they cannot speak
To say that their vows do not exist
challenge.explanation: Their vows are said to stand, without a husband’s authority being described over them.
challenge.q: Why are the vows of a widow and divorced woman presented separately?

answers: The passage refers both generally to vows and specifically to vows of personal affliction
The two expressions have no difference in the passage
challenge.explanation: The passage first speaks generally of vows and then specifically mentions binding oaths to afflict the soul.
challenge.q: What distinction appears between “every vow” and a vow “to afflict the soul”?

answers: He transfers them to the father
challenge.explanation: Verse 15 says that if he holds his peace, he establishes all her vows and bonds.
challenge.q: What is the result when the husband holds his peace from day to day?

paragraphs.title: Silence, Delayed Cancellation, and the Summary of the Laws

answers: It transfers the vow to the father
easy.explanation: The passage says that his silence establishes the vows.
easy.q: What does the husband’s silence do when he hears the vow?

answers: The vows return to her father
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “then he shall bear her iniquity.”
easy.q: What happens if the husband makes the vows void after he has heard them?

answers: Between a king and his people
Between a priest and a Levite
Between a man and his wife, and a father and his daughter
easy.explanation: Verse 17 summarizes the statutes as concerning a man and his wife and a father and his daughter.
easy.q: Between whom are these statutes summarized?

answers: The first is allowed in the passage, while the later action brings responsibility upon the husband
Canceling it on the day heard is always forbidden
medium.explanation: The passage permits disallowing the vow on the day it is heard but says that later cancellation makes the husband bear iniquity.
medium.q: What is the difference between canceling a vow on the day it is heard and canceling it later?

medium.explanation: To hold his peace means to remain silent rather than cancel the vow.
medium.q: What does “hold his peace” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: The final verse summarizes laws between husbands and wives and between fathers and daughters.
medium.q: What is the subject of the final verse?

answers: The timing of the decision has legal and moral significance
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes cancellation on the day of hearing from cancellation afterward and assigns responsibility for the later action.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the husband’s responsibility when he cancels a vow late?

answers: It gathers the laws around the relationships of father and daughter and husband and wife
It cancels all the preceding laws
It changes to an unrelated subject
challenge.explanation: The summary identifies the family relationships discussed throughout the passage.
challenge.q: How does the final verse connect with the earlier verses?

answers: Silence establishes the vow, but a later attempt to cancel it has a different consequence
Every kind of silence cancels the vow
Only the father’s silence is mentioned
challenge.explanation: The verses distinguish silence that establishes the vow from a later cancellation that brings responsibility upon the husband.
challenge.q: What detail about silence is easy to overlook?
